text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The Intellivision was released in 1979 by Mattel Electronics as a competitor to the Atari 2600. It was marketed as a more advanced console with improved graphics, a numeric keypad controller, and a focus on sports and strategy games. Its library included popular titles such as Astrosmash, Utopia, Advanced Dungeons & Dragons, Tron Deadly Discs, and Major League Baseball. Mattel developed a number of expansion devices, including the Intellivoice speech module and computer keyboard add-on. The system was known for its deeper gameplay experiences compared with many early consoles. Although it did not surpass Atari in sales, the Intellivision became one of the most successful second-generation systems and remains recognized for its unique controller and game design.
